coverageRationale.zh: 把 Crypto AG 事件写成供应链拦截模型：秘密所有权、弱化设备、销售覆盖、采集条件和工作因子下降；明确公开记录没有逐台算法复刻，公式只是分析模型。
coverageRationale.en: Formalizes the Crypto AG case as a supply-chain interception model: secret ownership, weakened devices, sales reach, collection conditions and work-factor reduction. It states that the public record does not reconstruct every device algorithm; the formulas are analytical only.

zh: Operation Rubicon / Thesaurus：CIA 与 BND 秘密控制 Crypto AG 的行动代号。
弱设备：加密强度被人为降低、可在现实工作量内破解的设备。
工作因子：破解所需试验次数或计算量。
采集条件：拥有设备、目标使用、通信可被收集三者同时成立。
en: Operation Rubicon / Thesaurus: the CIA–BND operation that secretly controlled Crypto AG.
Weak device: equipment whose encryption was deliberately weakened enough to break with realistic effort.
Work factor: the number of trials or computation needed to break the cipher.
Collection condition: ownership, target use and collectable traffic must all hold.

zh.principle: **攻击**：Crypto AG 后门（Crypto AG Backdoor）。Crypto AG 后门不是“某台机器里有一个秘密公式”，而是供应链控制：秘密拥有厂商、向客户销售“强/弱”两类设备、让弱设备的加密可以被现实工作量破解，再通过通信拦截把解密结果变成情报。把公开记录能支持的部分写成条件模型：P_read=P_own·P_use·P_collect。P_own 是目标使用的设备来自被控厂商的概率，P_use 是目标实际使用该设备的概率，P_collect 是相关通信可被采集的概率。三者缺一，后门不产生可读情报。工作因子侧可写：原始密钥空间 |K|=2^k，若设备被削弱 b 位，则 |K_eff|=2^(k-b)，相对工作因子 ρ=2^-b；给定 T 次试验解密，单次成功率 P_trial(T)=min(1,T/2^(k-b))。这只是把“变弱”折算成可计算量的分析模型，不是 Crypto AG 的真实算法复刻。
zh.why: 公开调查显示，这种控制的价值在于规模：一台设备卖到多国政府、军队和外交机构，同一类弱点就能被反复利用；而且客户看到的是“正常产品”，不会主动怀疑厂商。供应链后门因此比单次网络攻击更隐蔽、更持久。它同时暴露了安全边界：弱设备不只服务一国情报机构，也可能被第三方逆向或利用；出口管制、盟友关系和厂商声誉都会反噬。对采购方，信任链必须延伸到厂商所有权、代码/硬件来源和独立检测。
zh.used: 历史步骤：1952 年 Boris Hagelin 在瑞士创立 Crypto AG；1970 年 CIA 与西德 BND 秘密共同收购，行动代号 Thesaurus/Rubicon；向多国销售加密设备；对部分设备削弱算法；1993 年德方退出，CIA 继续控制；2018 年公司清算；2020 年联合调查公开。防御侧：对高价值通信不要依赖单一厂商的封闭算法；要求公开算法、独立审计、密钥托管透明和供应链溯源；对“异常便宜、异常好卖”的设备保持警惕。
zh.broken: 失效与边界：公开记录没有逐台设备的算法、密钥长度和客户清单，不能把任何具体设备都断言为已破解；P_read 是分析模型，不是历史统计；弱设备也会伤害盟友和本国私企；出口管制与政治反噬会削弱行动的长期收益。伦理与法律：这是情报行动史，不是可复制的攻击教程；不能据此推导现代设备的实现细节。对历史事件的兴趣应落在供应链治理、采购审计和加密透明度上。
zh.history:
Crypto AG 于 1952 年由 Boris Hagelin 在瑞士 Steinhausen 创立；1970 年被 CIA 与西德 BND 秘密收购，德方约 1993 年退出，CIA 作为唯一所有者持续到约 2018 年，公司随后清算。2020 年 2 月 Washington Post、ZDF 和 SRF 联合调查公开此事；瑞士议会 GPDel 于 2020 年 11 月发布报告，联邦委员会 2021 年 5 月作出回应。事件成为供应链信任与出口管制的经典案例。

en.principle: **Attack**: Crypto AG Backdoor (Crypto AG 后门). The Crypto AG backdoor was not “a secret formula inside one machine”. It was supply-chain control: secretly own the vendor, sell both “strong” and “weak” devices, make the weak devices breakable with realistic effort, and turn decryption into intelligence through communications interception. The public record supports a conditional model: P_read=P_own·P_use·P_collect. P_own is the chance the target's device came from the controlled vendor; P_use is the chance the target actually used it; P_collect is the chance the relevant traffic could be collected. Missing any one condition yields no readable intelligence. On the work-factor side, if the original key space is |K|=2^k and the device is weakened by b bits, then |K_eff|=2^(k-b) and the relative work factor is ρ=2^-b. With T trial decryptions, one-attempt success is P_trial(T)=min(1,T/2^(k-b)). This is an analytical conversion of “weaker” into computable effort, not a reconstruction of Crypto AG's actual algorithms.
en.why:
The public investigation shows that the value came from scale: one device sold to many governments, militaries and diplomatic services lets the same class of weakness be reused. Customers saw a “normal product” and had no reason to suspect the vendor. A supply-chain backdoor is therefore stealthier and more durable than a one-off cyberattack.

It also exposes a security boundary: weak devices do not serve only one intelligence service; third parties may reverse or exploit them; export controls, alliances and vendor reputation can backfire. For buyers, the trust chain must extend to vendor ownership, code/hardware provenance and independent testing.
en.used:
Historical steps: Boris Hagelin founded Crypto AG in Switzerland in 1952; the CIA and West German BND secretly bought it together in 1970 under Thesaurus/Rubicon; encryption devices were sold to many countries; some devices had weakened algorithms; the BND exited in 1993 and the CIA retained control; the company was liquidated in 2018; a joint investigation published the story in 2020.

Defense: do not rely on one vendor's closed algorithm for high-value traffic; require published algorithms, independent audit, transparent key management and supply-chain provenance; treat “unusually cheap or unusually available” devices with suspicion.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken:
Failure and boundaries: the public record does not contain per-device algorithms, key lengths or customer lists, so no specific device can be asserted broken; P_read is an analytical model, not a historical statistic; weak devices also harm allies and domestic firms; export controls and political blowback can erode the long-term gain.

Ethics and law: this is intelligence history, not a replicable attack tutorial; it must not be used to infer implementation details of modern devices. The useful lesson is supply-chain governance, procurement audit and cryptographic transparency.
en.history: Crypto AG was founded by Boris Hagelin in Steinhausen, Switzerland, in 1952. The CIA and West German BND secretly bought it in 1970; the BND exited around 1993 and the CIA remained sole owner until about 2018, after which the company was liquidated. In February 2020, the Washington Post, ZDF and SRF published a joint investigation. The Swiss Parliament's GPDel issued its report in November 2020 and the Federal Council responded in May 2021. The case became a classic study in supply-chain trust and export control.
